body:
Re-expanding a sorted SQLite Margin result now copies its public columns and retains its zero-row type anchor and carried declared-output types, preventing private sort-column leaks, mismatched UNION operands, and type loss during finite collection. PostgreSQL selected inputs are enclosed before expansion, keeping ORDER BY/LIMIT inside each grouping-set occurrence and copying the selected rows correctly.

SQLite direct collection and materialization keep the existing type and destination-safety boundaries. Source window-order metadata and construction-time laziness remain intact; this adds no guarantee that an earlier Margin order survives later ordinary verbs.

Fixes #976.
Fixes #977.

Validation:

- Public SQLite re-expansion matrix: one/multiple input grouping sets, empty inputs, no/included/rollup output plans, previous and new identifiers, all Margin orders, direct/finite collection, and materialization. Additional regressions cover special public names, changed inputs, collection class and fractional-limit behavior, and declaration overrides.
- PostgreSQL structural translation regression and live PostgreSQL 17.11 acceptance for head-only, arrange-only, combined, and collapsed inputs, NULL/string labels, occurrence identifiers, collection, materialization, window metadata, and construction-time laziness. The live runner is also wired into CI.
- Review-ready check: `9150a823ad05edbceb73a6adacc00376e89a45d5`
  - package spelling: passed

- [Code-review record](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/989#issuecomment-6484235042): Standards had no findings; both Spec findings were fixed in the final commit and independently verified. No unresolved findings. The fixed point is the merge-base with `main`, `d67edf81384b42816b8666f599f89c556d797682`.

## Standards

Initial review: no findings.

Follow-up: no new documented-standard violations or reportable Fowler smells.

## Spec

Initial review raised two P2 findings under #976:

1. Finite zero-row collection lost source-column types after re-expansion.
2. Prior declared-output types were dropped at the composition boundary.

Both were fixed in [9150a82](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/9150a823ad05edbceb73a6adacc00376e89a45d5). The [public re-expansion regressions](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/9150a823ad05edbceb73a6adacc00376e89a45d5/tests/testthat/test-sqlite-reexpansion.R) cover finite source types, previous identifiers, collection behavior, and declaration overrides.

Follow-up: both original reproductions were independently rerun against the installed final code and resolved. Additional checks passed for empty/nonempty inputs, NULL/string first-operation labels, all second-operation sort modes, finite collection, materialization, and a third expansion. No new findings within the focused review.

Totals: Standards 0 findings; Spec 2 resolved P2 findings, 0 unresolved. The final Review-ready invocation was still running during verification and was not treated as passed evidence.
